sentences.text: Avaceratops was a small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Northwest United States.
A second skull, MOR 692, which may not belong to Avaceratops, indicates a body length of 4.2 meters.
In 2010, Paul estimated that a four-meter-long Avaceratops would weigh one tonne.
The squamosal element at the front of the frill is large and features a continuously curving edge rather than a stepped one.
The first remains of Avaceratops were discovered in 1981 by Eddie Cole in the Judith River Formation of Montana on land owned by Arthur J. Lammers.
Avaceratops was formally named and described by Peter Dodson in 1986 as the type species Avaceratops lammersi.
The genus name Avaceratops honors Eddie Cole's wife, Ava Cole.
The specific epithet lammersi honors the Lammers family, who owned the land where the fossils were found.
In 1993, Paul Penkalski referred two earlier discovered squamosals belonging to larger individuals to Avaceratops.
In 1999, Penkalski and Dodson described a second skull, MOR 692, which belonged to a larger individual.
Avaceratops was a herbivore, feeding on plants like ferns, cycads, and conifers that were predominant during the Cretaceous.
Like all ceratopsians, Avaceratops was a herbivore.
The animal likely used its sharp beak to bite leaves or needles from plants.
Dodson assigned Avaceratops to the family Ceratopsidae within the order Ceratopsia in 1986.
A 2013 phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. found Avaceratops to be the sister taxon of the genus Nasutoceratops.
A phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. in 2013 found that Avaceratops was the sister taxon to the newly described genus Nasutoceratops.
The clade containing Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops was named Nasutoceratopsini in 2016.
Avaceratops lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 80 million years ago, during the Campanian stage in what is now North America.
Avaceratops lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Avaceratops lived in a heavily forested and wet habitat.
The habitat of Avaceratops was primarily wet forests.
